matching_criterion: Seasonal allergic rhinitis (hay fever) due to pollen. Any wording that names allergic rhinitis / hay fever counts as correct; viral rhinitis, bacterial sinusitis or non-allergic rhinitis as the final diagnosis does not.

management_reference.management: Intranasal corticosteroids are the pharmacological treatment of choice for allergic rhinitis.
management_reference.source_quote: Intranasal corticosteroids are the pharmacological treatment of choice for all forms of AR

management_reference.management: Do not use first-generation (sedating) antihistamines for routine management.
management_reference.source_quote: strongly discourages the use of first-generation AH in the routine management of AR

management_reference.management: Encourage saline sprays or rinses, regularly and before the intranasal steroid.
management_reference.source_quote: The use of saline sprays or rinses is effective to remove mucus, allergens and inflammatory cells, and regular use, preceding the use of INCS, should be encouraged

management_reference.management: Allergen avoidance: avoid outdoor activities and wear masks during peak pollen periods, keep doors and windows closed, change clothing when returning home.
management_reference.source_quote: Keep doors and windows closed.Change clothing when returning home

management_scoring_note: Only items with a verified source quote are scored; general good practice that the article does not state is not scored.
